notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) subsystem, specifically within the `rxe` driver. An error in the `rxe_srq_from_init` function's memory management can lead to a double free vulnerability. This occurs when an attempt to copy data to user space fails, causing the same memory region to be freed twice. A local attacker could potentially exploit this flaw to cause a denial of service (DoS) by crashing the system.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

The system must be rebooted for this update to take effect.

To mitigate this vulnerability, prevent the `rdma_rxe` kernel module from loading. Create a file `/etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-rdma_rxe.conf` with `blacklist rdma_rxe`. Regenerate the initramfs using `sudo dracut -f -v` (or `sudo mkinitrd -f -v /boot/initramfs-$(uname -r).img $(uname -r)` for older systems) and reboot. This action may impact functionality dependent on the RDMA/rxe driver.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's RDMA/mlx4 component. This vulnerability arises from the incorrect use of Read-Copy Update (RCU) in the `mlx4_srq_event()` function. An attacker could potentially trigger an event before the `srq` object is fully initialized, leading to a system crash. This could result in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected system.

notes.text:

Additionally, this issue can cause an unexpected process crash but the possibility of remote code execution is not discarded.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

vulnerabilities.title: chromium-browser: angle: Out of bounds memory access in ANGLE

notes.text: A flaw was found in chromium-browser. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists within the ANGLE graphics component, allowing a remote attacker to trigger out-of-bounds memory access by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This allows an attacker to potentially manipulate memory contents. The vulnerability is triggered by processing malicious graphics instructions. This can lead to unexpected program behavior.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

vulnerabilities.title: chromium-browser: angle: ANGLE: Arbitrary code execution via use after free

notes.text: A flaw was found in ANGLE, a component of Google Chrome on Android. This 'use after free' vulnerability allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code outside the browser's security sandbox. This can be exploited by enticing a user to visit a specially crafted HTML page. Successful exploitation could lead to a complete compromise of the affected device.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

vulnerabilities.title: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: Use after free in Skia

notes.text: A flaw was found in ANGLE, a component within Google Chrome on Android. This out-of-bounds write vulnerability allows a remote attacker to potentially perform a sandbox escape by enticing a user to visit a specially crafted HTML page. This could lead to an attacker executing arbitrary code outside the browser's security sandbox.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: angle: ANGLE: Sandbox escape via out-of-bounds write in Google Chrome on Android
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important flaw in the ANGLE component of Chromium allows a remote attacker to achieve a sandbox escape. Exploitation requires user interaction, where a victim must visit a specially crafted HTML page, enabling an attacker to execute arbitrary code outside the browser's security sandbox. This bypasses security boundaries, leading to potential compromise of the underlying system.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used in Google Chrome. A remote attacker, after compromising the renderer process, could exploit an uninitialized use vulnerability by crafting a malicious HTML page. This could lead to the disclosure of sensitive cross-origin data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Information disclosure via uninitialized use in Google Chrome
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity information disclosure flaw was found in Skia, the 2D graphics library used by Google Chrome and by WebKitGTK in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. An uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the browser's renderer process to leak cross-origin data when a user visits a crafted HTML page. Red Hat assessed this flaw as having moderate impact rather than upstream's High rating because exploitation requires the attacker to have already compromised the renderer process, so the flaw primarily enables information disclosure across the same-origin policy boundary rather than an initial compromise. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, 8, and 9, the webkit2gtk3 and webkitgtk4 components that bundle Skia are affected, and fixes are being pursued through the upstream WebKitGTK project; Red Hat's Firefox and Thunderbird packages are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in the Skia copies they ship. The chromium package in Fedora and EPEL (Community Projects) is also affected, with updates handled through the community channels.

notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Cross-origin data leakage via uninitialized use
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of important impact was found in Skia, the graphics library used by Chromium and bundled in WebKit-based rendering engines. Uninitialized memory use in Skia allows a remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process to leak sensitive cross-origin data when the victim views a crafted HTML page, bypassing the same-origin policy and exposing confidential data across origins. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux the flaw is reachable through the webkit2gtk3 component, and a fix is being pursued for the affected streams. Firefox in Red Hat Enterprise Linux is not affected because the vulnerable code is not in the execute path, and Thunderbird and the webkitgtk4 package in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present. The community-maintained chromium and webkitgtk packages in Fedora and EPEL are also affected, and fixes are pursued through those channels. Red Hat rated this flaw Important (CVSS 7.4), which is consistent with the upstream Chromium severity of High; CISA assigned a lower CVSS score (3.1, Low), reflecting high attack complexity, low confidentiality impact, and unchanged scope in its vector.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library. A remote attacker, who has already compromised the renderer process, could exploit a use-after-free vulnerability by providing a specially crafted HTML page. This could lead to the execution of arbitrary code within the sandbox environment, potentially allowing further system compromise.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: chromium-browser: skia: chromium-browser: skia: Arbitrary code execution via crafted HTML page
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity use-after-free flaw was found in Skia, a 2D graphics library used for graphics rendering in web browsers and email clients, affecting multiple Red Hat products. A remote attacker who has already compromised the renderer process of an application using Skia could exploit this flaw by tricking a user into loading a specially crafted HTML page, triggering a use-after-free that allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code within the application's sandbox and potentially achieve further system compromise. Because exploitation requires the attacker to already control the renderer process, Red Hat scores this flaw with a local attack vector and scope change (CVSS 8.2, IMPORTANT), while upstream Google rates the corresponding Chromium issue as High severity. Red Hat products that bundle affected Skia code are impacted, including the chromium, firefox, thunderbird, and webkitgtk component families across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Fedora, and EPEL; Thunderbird in the RHEL 8 BRP is not affected. Fixes for the affected products are being pursued.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text: A flaw was found in WebKitGTK. Processing malicious web content can cause an unexpected process crash due to improper memory handling.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: webkitgtk: Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to an unexpected process crash
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
To exploit this issue, an attacker needs to trick a user into processing or loading malicious web content. Due to this reason, this flaw has been rated with an important severity.
Additionally, this issue can cause an unexpected process crash but the possibility of remote code execution is not discarded.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text: A flaw was found in WebKitGTK. Processing malicious web content can cause an unexpected process crash due to improper memory handling.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: webkitgtk: Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to an unexpected process crash
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
To exploit this issue, an attacker needs to trick a user into processing or loading malicious web content. Due to this reason, this flaw has been rated with an important severity.
Additionally, this issue can cause an unexpected process crash but the possibility of remote code execution is not discarded.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

Do not process or load untrusted web content with WebKitGTK.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, the following packages require WebKitGTK4: evolution-data-server, glade, gnome-boxes, gnome-initial-setup, gnome-online-accounts, gnome-shell, shotwell, sushi and yelp.

This vulnerability can only be exploited when these packages are installed in the system and being used via a graphical interface to process untrusted web content, via GNOME for example. In gnome-shell, the vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker from the local network without user interaction.

To mitigate this vulnerability, consider removing these packages. Note that some of these packages are required by GNOME, removing them will also remove GNOME and other packages, breaking functionality. However, the server can still be used via the terminal interface.

Additionally, WebKitGTK3 is not required by any package. Therefore, it can be removed without consequences or break of functionality.

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenJDK. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted requests across network protocols to exposed application programming interfaces (APIs) within the Security component. A successful attack can result in unauthorized modification, creation, or deletion of critical application data. In addition, the flaw may allow untrusted code running in a restricted sandbox environment to tamper with protected data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: openjdk: Enhance PKCS5 padding (Oracle CPU 2026-10)
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact because exploitation carries high complexity, requiring targeted conditions where an application exposes PKCS#5 cryptographic padding routines directly to unauthenticated network input. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux and container deployments, Java applications do not process raw cipher data from untrusted clients without intermediate validation layers or authentication. Furthermore, the scope is limited to data integrity without compromising confidentiality or causing service denial.

Consequently, the operational risk in standard environments is minimal.

Earlier Java LTS versions in Red Hat Enterprise Linux do not contain the vulnerable compilation routines, limiting exposure to newer runtime releases.

notes.text: The certificate authority (CA) store used in OpenJDK and Oracle Java included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL Java client applications and cause such applications to connect to malicious sites.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: OpenJDK: Distrust eMudhra intermediate CA certificates due to security concerns
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
The non-portable OpenJDK RPM packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux rely on ca-certificates packages for their default certificate store. Therefore, those OpenJDK versions require updated ca-certificates RPM package to be installed to address this issue (refer to CVE-2026-114406 for more details).

The portable OpenJDK builds for both Linux and Windows include their own certificate store and therefore need to be updated separately from the ca-certificates updates.

The certificate bundle in OpenJDK upstream included root certificates, which signed eMudhra certificates with weak keys. Upstream OpenJDK fix did not initially remove those root certificates, but rather only blocked problematic intermediate certificates. However, this fix was found to be insufficient and OpenJDK upstream later removed relevant root CA certificates, see CVE-2026-114820.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: openjdk: Enhance HTTP server (Oracle CPU 2026-10)
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact for Red Hat products because, although it can be triggered remotely without authentication or user interaction, successful exploitation is limited to partial data integrity alterations without compromising confidentiality or system availability. Java runtime environments across Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Red Hat OpenJDK distributions are exposed when hosting web applications or network endpoints that parse untrusted requests via built-in HTTP server APIs. Due to inconsistent request processing, an external attacker submitting malformed requests can manipulate accessible data flows, but the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution or broader infrastructure compromise.

vulnerabilities.title: openjdk: Enhance Certificate Constraint Checking (Oracle CPU 2026-10)

notes.text: The certificate authority (CA) store used in OpenJDK and Oracle Java included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL Java client applications and cause such applications to connect to malicious sites.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: OpenJDK: Distrust eMudhra intermediate CA certificates due to security concerns
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
The non-portable OpenJDK RPM packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux rely on ca-certificates packages for their default certificate store. Therefore, those OpenJDK versions require updated ca-certificates RPM package to be installed to address this issue (refer to CVE-2026-114406 for more details).

The portable OpenJDK builds for both Linux and Windows include their own certificate store and therefore neeed to be updated separately from the ca-certificates updates.

notes.text: The certificate authority (CA) store used in OpenJDK and Oracle Java included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL Java client applications and cause such applications to connect to malicious sites.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: OpenJDK: Distrust eMudhra intermediate CA certificates due to security concerns
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
The non-portable OpenJDK RPM packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux rely on ca-certificates packages for their default certificate store. Therefore, those OpenJDK versions require updated ca-certificates RPM package to be installed to address this issue (refer to CVE-2026-114406 for more details).

The portable OpenJDK builds for both Linux and Windows include their own certificate store and therefore need to be updated separately from the ca-certificates updates.

The certificate bundle in OpenJDK upstream included root certificates, which signed eMudhra certificates with weak keys. Upstream OpenJDK fix did not initially remove those root certificates, but rather only blocked problematic intermediate certificates. However, this fix was found to be insufficient and OpenJDK upstream later removed relevant root CA certificates, see CVE-2026-114820.

vulnerabilities.title: openjdk: Enhance Certificate Constraint Checking (Oracle CPU 2026-10)

notes.text: The certificate authority (CA) store used in OpenJDK and Oracle Java included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL Java client applications and cause such applications to connect to malicious sites.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: OpenJDK: Distrust eMudhra intermediate CA certificates due to security concerns
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
The non-portable OpenJDK RPM packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux rely on ca-certificates packages for their default certificate store. Therefore, those OpenJDK versions require updated ca-certificates RPM package to be installed to address this issue (refer to CVE-2026-114406 for more details).

The portable OpenJDK builds for both Linux and Windows include their own certificate store and therefore neeed to be updated separately from the ca-certificates updates.
